response.final_answer:
$\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CDE$ by ASA:
$$\angle BAE \cong \angle DCE \text{ (alt. interior } \angle\text{s, } \overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}\text{)}, \quad \overline{AE} \cong \overline{CE} \text{ (given)}, \quad \angle AEB \cong \angle CED \text{ (vert. } \angle\text{s)}$$

steps.description:
We have two triangles, $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle CDE$, that share the point $E$ in the middle. We're given two facts:
- $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$ (the two segments are parallel)
- $\overline{AE} \cong \overline{CE}$ (one pair of sides is already equal)

The elegant path here is **ASA** (Angle-Side-Angle): find one angle on each side of the known equal sides $AE$ and $CE$. The parallel lines will hand us one pair of angles for free via **alternate interior angles**, and the shared crossing point $E$ gives us another pair via **vertical angles**.
steps.title: Understand the Setup

steps.description:
Line $\overline{AC}$ acts as a **transversal** crossing the parallel lines $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$.

When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, the **alternate interior angles** are equal — they sit on opposite sides of the transversal, between the parallel lines.

Here, $\angle BAE$ and $\angle DCE$ are alternate interior angles formed by transversal $\overline{AC}$ and parallels $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$:
$$\angle BAE \cong \angle DCE$$
steps.title: Alternate Interior Angles

steps.description:
At point $E$, segments $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{CE}$ form two straight lines crossing each other. The angles on opposite sides of that intersection are **vertical angles**, which are always congruent:
$$\angle AEB \cong \angle CED$$

Now we have an angle, the given side, and another angle — all lined up for ASA.
steps.title: Vertical Angles at E

steps.description:
Assembling everything for $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle CDE$:

| | $\triangle ABE$ | $\triangle CDE$ | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Angle | $\angle BAE$ | $\angle DCE$ | Alternate interior angles, $\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}$ |
| Side | $\overline{AE}$ | $\overline{CE}$ | Given |
| Angle | $\angle AEB$ | $\angle CED$ | Vertical angles |

The two angles are on **either side of the included side** $AE = CE$, so by **ASA** (Angle-Side-Angle):
$$\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CDE \qquad \blacksquare$$
steps.title: Conclude by ASA
